mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO), manufacturing supply constraints intensify, leading to higher input costs and reduced corporate margins, which cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS grows, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stagflationary pressures that reduce real corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and INDPRO falls, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
